scope: Read-only audit of the original SH3, the earlier 35 x 35 SH3 W-grid, the active-BGO-small-aperture 25 x 25 SH3 grid used by package 72, and the SG3B comparison geometry. No transport was launched and no existing artifact was overwritten.
headline_conclusion: The 3.796 cm active-BGO square aperture was implemented and used correctly, but it is not the dominant acceptance for the surviving monoenergetic 511-keV background. It strongly suppresses the removed outer annulus locally, while most selected events reach the TES through uncollided BGO transmission or zero-energy-loss Rayleigh paths. Therefore the total selected rate is not expected to scale with the gross square-hole area.

important_semantic_correction.statement: A recorded BGO energy deposit of 0 keV does not mean that the primary trajectory did not cross or interact in BGO.
mechanisms: A 510.99895-keV photon can traverse a finite BGO thickness without a discrete interaction and then deposit its full energy in the TES.
A photon can undergo Rayleigh elastic scattering in BGO, retain the line energy, leave no BGO energy deposit, and then enter the TES.
important_semantic_correction.analysis_implication: The equality of the W2 pre-veto and active-BGO-veto counts is not evidence that the surviving photons avoided the BGO geometry.

why_gross_area_scaling_is_invalid: The new BGO square is still larger than the 3.6 x 3.6 cm TES layer envelope.

The central 25 x 25 pitch-and-web pattern is the same pattern used by SG3B and is the central subset of the earlier 35 x 35 SH3 grid; the removed peripheral channels do not map one-to-one onto the TES projection.
At normal incidence the relevant projected acceptance is limited by the TES footprint and grid open fraction, not by the unused 6 x 6 cm outer BGO hole.
At finite angles, transmission and elastic-scattering paths through BGO and W also survive without an active-veto energy deposit.

other_serial_features.note: The 2.7 cm-radius mechanical-Al opening is larger than the active-BGO square but is in series with it; it does not bypass the 3.796 cm BGO cut. The rear 0.75 cm port is a separate reverse-entry path.

collimation_lever_arm.interpretation: The same 0.798 cm-deep 25 x 25 grid has approximately four times the grid-to-detector angular lever arm in SG3B. The close SH3 grid therefore does not reproduce the SG3B angular acceptance even though the grid pitch, web, square envelope, and TES footprint match.

sh3.description: Compact BGO cylinder around the TES stack with a front square cut and a rear circular cold-port cut.

sg3b.description: Large full-wrap BGO topology plus separate end structures and the same 3.796 cm side-window cut.

bgo_topology_comparison.interpretation: Equal TES area and equal nominal square-window size do not make the SH3 and SG3B shielding/acceptance geometries equivalent.

current_small_aperture_w2_pre_veto_path_.population: All 54 events passing the model-B [510.58, 511.42) keV pre-veto window in the 5,000,000-photon package-72 trial
current_small_aperture_w2_pre_veto_path_.classification_method: IA INIT and all pre-TES IA records were read from the 21 raw SIM.gz files. World coordinates were transformed to InstrumentFrame local coordinates using the retained +45 degree y rotation. Straight paths were intersected with the exact front, side, and rear BGO solids.

current_small_aperture_w2_final_path_cro.interpretation: Even geometric intersection with a W bar is not an absorption guarantee; the selected sample is conditioned on the rare full-energy survivors.

old_large_aperture_wgrid_to_current_smal.interpretation: The aperture reduction works where it is geometrically supposed to work: the removed annulus falls by about 70%. It cannot drive a 60% total-rate reduction because that annulus supplied only about 14% of the earlier selected population.

total_rate_comparison.statistical_conclusion: No significant total-rate worsening or improvement is resolved by the present trial. The apparent increase is a 0.48-sigma fluctuation.

diagnostic_verdict.supported_explanation: The large SH3 front opening contributed a minor removable annulus component, but the dominant difference is not its gross area. The short SH3 grid-to-TES distance, compact shielding topology, uncollided transmission through BGO/W, and zero-energy-loss Rayleigh redirection create surviving paths that an energy-deposit veto and a smaller outer window do not remove.
diagnostic_verdict.next_discriminating_test_if_needed: For a higher-precision causal decomposition, run matched-statistics tagged transport or forced-interaction/path-length scoring for the retained-square, removed-annulus, side-BGO, and rear-BGO categories. No such extra run is required to reject gross-area proportional scaling.
